findings.passage: Yet in a decade of interviews about the films that went wrong, she has never described a set as a place where she was misled or left unprotected. Her complaint, every time, is the one she gave at Cannes: the movie that reached the screen was not the movie she signed up to make.
findings.problem: The thesis is written as an absolute over her entire public record ("never," "every time"), and the record was not exhausted: research lists the Good Hang with Amy Poehler episode (June 10, 2025) as unopened, along with the Telegraph 2015, Vogue UK 2016 and Glamour UK 2017 originals. The opened Variety interview of July 7, 2025 (S45) also has her saying "I can't waste time on toxic sets anymore," a line that is not inventoried in the claims and that a reader could take as describing a set where she was not protected. One future interview framing a set as unsafe falsifies the sentence outright, and because it is the test the profile rests on, the only repair would be rewriting the thesis. The same absolute recurs in "Every fear she names is circumstantial" and in the Type 6 FAQ ("never that she was misled or left unprotected"). C95's reopen trigger is right; the prose should be written so it stays true as the record grows.
findings.acceptance_test: The thesis sentence, the "Every fear she names is circumstantial" sentence and the Type 6 FAQ are scoped to the reviewed record (for example, "In none of the interviews reviewed here, from 2015 to 2026, has she described a set as a place where she was misled or left unprotected" and "Every fear she names in this record is circumstantial"); the July 2025 "toxic sets" line is inventoried as a claim and either addressed in the body (as a statement about collaborators rather than about being misled) or recorded in the evidence as considered and why it does not change the read; C95 and C204 keep their reopen triggers and their claim text records the scope.

findings.passage: the other party to her central dispute has not answered
findings.problem: This sentence in the limits paragraph depends on the same unresolved fact as "As of October 8, 2026, no public response from James to either later account had been found" (C70) and the Fifty Shades FAQ (C205), but it is not covered by either claim's passage or trigger. If E.L. James responds, a refresh guided by C70 would update the dated sentence and the FAQ and leave this one stale and false.
findings.acceptance_test: C70's review_trigger (or a new claim) names this sentence as a third place to update, so that one trigger covers the dated body sentence, the limits paragraph and the FAQ; no prose change is required otherwise.

findings.passage: On the small feature she planned to direct in 2025, written with Vanessa Burghardt:
findings.problem: "planned to direct in 2025" reads as a 2025 shoot. The source (Variety, July 7, 2025) says she was getting ready to shoot, and the research notes an unused "July 2026 plan" claim, which suggests the film was still a plan a year later. A reader in 2029 cannot tell whether the film was ever made, and the Four argument built on "I can see this world" does not need the production status at all. C180 is time_sensitive with the right trigger, but the prose pins the year to the wrong verb.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence dates the statement rather than the production (for example, "On the small feature she said in July 2025 she was preparing to direct, written with Vanessa Burghardt"), says nothing about whether it was shot unless the accuracy check established that, and C180's passage is updated to match.

findings.passage: In February 2024 the superhero film _Madame Web_ opened; Wikipedia calls it "critically and commercially unsuccessful."
findings.problem: A verbatim quotation of a live wiki page's current wording, linked without a retrieval date. The phrasing will change, so a later reader following the link may not find the quoted words, and a mutable tertiary page is the weakest kind of citation for a characterization. The fact is uncontested and the Bustle context already carries it ("Asked about its reviews"). The two other Wikipedia attributions (the 1999 debut, the trilogy gross) are stable facts and age fine.
findings.acceptance_test: The Wikipedia quotation is replaced by a dated contemporaneous report of the film's reception or box office (February to March 2024) or by neutral prose that needs no quotation (for example, "opened to poor reviews and weak box office"), and C138's source_ids and passage are updated accordingly.

findings.passage: In spring 2026 she produced and starred in Alice Rohrwacher's _Three Incestuous Sisters_, shot on Stromboli and in Rome
findings.problem: An unreleased film with no distributor date is named with a final-looking italic title, while Johnson's own quote in the same paragraph calls it "Three Sisters." Pre-release titles change often, and C43's trigger covers the release date and reception but not the title. The Stromboli shoot is the durable evidence; the title is the fragile part.
findings.acceptance_test: C43's review_trigger adds "confirm the release title," and the prose either attributes the title to its source ("the film Vogue reported as Three Incestuous Sisters") or keeps the italic title with that trigger recorded; the editor may reject the prose change if the trigger alone is judged sufficient.

findings.passage: Accepting a depression-advocacy award in November 2023, she described a low day her partner caught before she did:
findings.problem: "her partner" is undated relative to the reader's present. The linked ¡HOLA! headline names Chris Martin, and the evidence record (S16) notes the couple split in June 2025. The draft rightly leaves the name out, but a reader in 2029 will take "her partner" as current unless the sentence says otherwise. C183 is marked stable with no trigger, which is fine for a historical anecdote once the prose is time-fixed.
findings.acceptance_test: The phrase reads "her partner at the time" (or equivalent), no name is added, and C183's passage is updated to match.

protected_passages.passage: "I found myself as an actor, a few times, showing up to the premiere of a movie to see it the first time," she said. Her verdict on those nights: "That is not what I thought we were making."
protected_passages.reason: A dated, sourced hook (Cannes, May 2025) that describes a repeated pattern ("a few times") rather than a current event. It will still be the right opening in 2031 and it is the Durability 9 anchor in practice.

protected_passages.passage: As of October 8, 2026, no public response from James to either later account had been found.
protected_passages.reason: The model of a dated unresolved statement with a matching trigger (C70). It keeps the Fifty Shades section fair to a named living person and makes the maintenance step obvious.

protected_passages.passage: If one does, its shape will matter: a fight framed as being misled or left unprotected would point toward Six, one framed as the work made false toward Four.
protected_passages.reason: A built-in settle signal that tells a future editor exactly what evidence would move the read. This sentence is what makes the page reopenable instead of merely dated.

protected_passages.passage: Plenty of actors grieve a wrap, and a Six could mourn the loss of a secure group. What is hers is the count, more times than she can number by her own account, and what ends.
protected_passages.reason: The close uses the latest interview (July 2026) but rests on a self-reported recurring pattern, so removing the Verity context leaves it intact, and it keeps the Six alternative live to the last paragraph.

protected_passages.passage: and the vow was gone: "There's no part of me that's like, 'Oh, I'll never do that again' to anything. I've done even tiny movies that didn't do well. Who cares?"
protected_passages.reason: A dated 2024-to-2025 reversal that survives the type argument and ages well because both tellings are dated. It is the kind of contradiction the standard asks to preserve rather than smooth over.

assessment: Five-year test: passes on substance. The central discriminator (fear named freely, grievance about the work made false) rests on Vanity Fair 2022, Vogue 2017, Marie Claire 2020, Bustle and L'Officiel 2024 and LA Times/Cannes 2025; removing the latest event (the Vogue October 2026 cover and Verity) costs the close its final quote and a few supporting lines ("I just want to be authentic," the womb-like set, "everyone is a spy") but not the argument. Verity and Three Incestuous Sisters appear for orientation only, as the research asked. Dates are absolute throughout; the only relative words ("now," "still") sit inside quotations. The Type 6 alternative is argued from dated evidence rather than from her current mood, so a later run that settles on Six would find the record it needs here. The hook and the close both describe repeated patterns rather than a comeback or a current title. The one consequential durability defect is that the thesis sentence is written as an absolute over an unexhausted record (future-01); scoped to the reviewed interviews it degrades gracefully, as written it can be falsified by a single new interview. The evidence record's time_sensitive and unresolved claims (C43, C70, C95, C113, C115, C156, C157, C170, C180, C205) carry actionable triggers; the gaps are small (future-02 through future-06): one untracked echo of the James non-response, an ambiguous year on the directing project, a live-wiki quotation, an unreleased title, and an undated "her partner." "Best known for the Fifty Shades of Grey films" is a status claim but a safe one over five years. Similarity diagnostic: every tripped pair is a self-match against the previous dakota-johnson draft in the same run; the highest cross-subject score (0.053, jeremy-allen-white) is a generic "cannot settle" phrase, not reused argument. Risk flags unchanged from the evidence record; nothing from the future seat warrants escalation.
